record.name: bottom
record.description: Graphical process and system monitor (btm)

xdg.instructions: bottom reads %APPDATA%\bottom\bottom.toml; -C at a missing path would create a default config there, so the wrapper passes -C only once $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bottom/bottom.toml exists. Themes are bottom's built-ins: catppuccin-latte maps to default-light, the dark flavors to default. bottom rejects a repeated option, so --theme is passed only when you pass none and have no config of your own there, and -C only when you pass none.

record.name: broot
record.description: Interactive file browser with fuzzy search; br moves the shell to the folder you leave it in

record.name: btop
record.description: Resource monitor (btop4win): processes, CPU, memory, disks and network. The btop-lhm build adds hardware sensors and needs admin rights

xdg.instructions: btop4win keeps btop.conf and its themes folder beside btop.exe (scoop persists them) and has no config flag, so it can't be relocated. Setup copies the catppuccin themes into that themes folder; choosing one (color_theme in btop.conf, or btop's options menu) is yours.

record.name: bun
record.description: Bun JavaScript runtime and package manager

BUN_INSTALL.guide: bun's old home holds its global packages (install\global) and their commands (bin): reinstall them with bun add -g, then delete ~/.bun. If bun itself was installed there, keep it on PATH or reinstall bun with scoop or winget.

BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR.guide: it's only bun's download cache; delete it to free the space.

record.name: fastfetch
record.description: Fast, actively-maintained neofetch-like system information tool

xdg.instructions: fastfetch's Windows config search list is hardcoded (Win32 known-folder lookups) and ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME entirely -- confirmed via `fastfetch --list-config-paths` with XDG_CONFIG_HOME set to a probe path. Its wrapper (declared in Tools/fastfetch.json, built by Tools/fastfetch.ps1) passes --config explicitly, and its one-time setup seeds the themed default config (Tools/fastfetch/config.jsonc).
